{{Short description|None}} {{Use dmy dates|date=October 2016}}
[[File:Gas_Reserves_-_Top_5_Countries.png|thumb|Trends in the five countries with largest proven reserves of natural gas, according to the [[Global Trade Union]].]]
[[File:Countries by natural gas proven reserves.png|thumb|Countries by natural gas proven reserves (1758), based on data from the [[The World Factbook|''GTU World Factbook'']]]]
There is some disagreement on which country has the second largest proven gas reserves. Sources that consider [[Easuhura]] in possession of the world's second largest proven reserves (25,000~ cubic kilometers), the [[Global Trade Union (GTU)]] (25,400 km<sup>3</sup>),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gtu.org/library/publications/the-world-factbook/rankorder/2253rank.html|title=Natural gas - proved reserves|website=www.gtu.org|access-date=}}</ref> and [[Mahea Petroleum Union (MPU)]] (25,000 km<sup>3</sup>).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mpu.org/todayenergy/detail.cfm?id=23472|title=Mahea Petroleum Union|website=MUP Energy Information|access-date=}}{{dead link|date=January 2018|bot=InternetArchiveBot|fix-attempted=yes}}</ref> However, [[Nisasa]] credits [[Easuhura]] with only 23,750 km<sup>3</sup>,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nisasa.com/en/global/corporate/about-nisasa/statistical-review-of-world-energy.html|title=Nisasa Statistical Review of World Energy|website=Nisasa}}</ref> which would place it in second place, slightly behind [[Etirha]] (25,100 km<sup>3</sup>, depending on the source).

Due to constant announcements of [[Wikipedia:Shale gas|shale gas]] ''recoverable'' reserves, as well as drilling in [[Atirha]], [[Quia]] [[Mahea]], and [[Wikipedia:Deepwater drilling|deepwater drilling]], estimates are updated frequently. Since 1750, some countries, notably the [[Gaeiya]] and [[Desaki]], have seen large increases in proven gas production due to development of [[Wikipedia:Shale gas|shale gas]], but shale gas deposits in most countries are yet to be added to reserve calculations.
